prompt: Use case: art-direction design for the top of a skate start tower in a stylized open-world game. Image 1 is a plain 3D render: a square timber start deck about 22 by 16 m high on a Kiyomizu-style timber frame over a volcano crater, flat-shaded and untextured, with a small placeholder pavilion roof on it. Paint it as the finished in-game scene. Keep its camera, horizon and field of view, and keep the deck, the long plank roll-in leaving it, the huge curved wooden wall beside it and the timber frame below exactly where and how they are. Image 2 is the approved art direction: copy its look exactly: soft painterly style, warm light, warm wooden skate ramps with thin steel coping, massive weathered hinoki pillars with nuki tie-beams and stone footings, red-lacquer accents, dark volcanic rock with moss, a little snow on the ground only, never on a ramp. HARD RULE: the deck is where riders start: they run and roll across its whole surface and off its edges onto both ramps, so nothing may stand on the deck surface or in front of either ramp's start. Posts may only rise from the timber frame below, outside the deck's edges, or stand at the deck's outer corners on the railing line; anything overhead stays at least 6 m above the deck so it frames the riders, never blocks them. Remove the placeholder pavilion. Design: the deck becomes the open floor of a hilltop temple stage: a broad sweeping irimoya hip-and-gable roof with dark tiles, upturned eaves and red-lacquered bracket sets, carried high above the deck on four massive corner pillars only, at the deck's outer corners; open on every side so riders roll out from under the eaves, with hanging bronze lanterns at the eave corners and red nobori banners on the railing.
purpose: Crater Park editor park art direction
